A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CROSS framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original temporal link prediction and industrial fraud classification results, together with ablations, robustness experiments, and a case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds further metric results, an additional baseline, representation analyses, and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The temporal reasoning chain, semantic and structural layers, cross-modal mixer, output construction, and training loss remain unchanged in Equations 1–11 and Algorithm 1. Expanded explanations and additional LLM ablations do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Enron, GDELT, ICEWS1819, Googlemap_CT, and Industrial for the same link prediction and fraud classification tasks. Added analyses use existing coverage. Correcting the swapped Enron/GDELT descriptions does not indicate different datasets, and the conflict discussion does not document a distinct new input scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds LKD4DyTAG to the temporal link prediction comparison in Table 1 while retaining the earlier comparators. Figure 3's classification comparator set is unchanged. GPT-4o is added as an internal LLM ablation, not a competing standalone method.

E3.justification: v2 adds AUC and Hits@10 evaluation for link prediction on Enron and ICEWS1819, a GPT-4o configuration, and a performance-versus-training-time evaluation. The chronological 60/20/20 splits, 100 evaluation negatives, training budgets, dimensions, and existing robustness settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary analysis with representation-distribution case studies concerning modality alignment and conflicts (Figures 10 and 19), plus performance/training-time trade-offs across four datasets (Figure 13). It also extends the LLM ablation with GPT-4o. Existing perturbation, depth, component, textual-input, and reasoning-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces kernel density estimation of representation distributions in Appendix A, adding a descriptive statistical estimation procedure. Benchmark uncertainty reporting remains three runs with seeds 0–2 and means with standard deviations; the density plots do not provide additional uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive AUC/Hits@10 results in Table 6, LKD4DyTAG scores, GPT-4o results, representation findings, and training-time and industrial LLM-cost measurements. Table 1 changes FreeDyG's inductive MRR on Googlemap_CT from 76.01 to 66.01 and Industrial from 76.48 to 56.48. The existing CROSS MRR scores, classification AUC results, and earlier ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, Theorem 1, its integrity/complementarity assumptions, and the proof in Appendix B are unchanged. The complexity analysis moves from Appendix I.1 to L.2 without changing its mathematical substance.

C1.justification: v2 changes the problem framing from 'unexplored' to 'under-explored' and explicitly claims the first framework unifying semantics and structures with LLMs for TTAG modeling. The central contribution is retained, and the existing 24.7% and 3.7% gains are clarified as absolute MRR and AUC gains rather than new performance improvements.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations linking feature-distribution differences to complementarity and overlapping distributions to successful unification. Appendix L.1 extends the applicability argument to conflicting modalities using the new visualization and existing noise tests; Appendices G–H strengthen the industrial scalability argument. The previously stated limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 corrects the swapped dataset-description labels, identifies WeChat as the industrial source, and documents GPT-4o API use. It adds industrial token, time, and monetary costs in Table 7 and training-time measurements in Figure 13. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and conditional plans to release generated texts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges LKD4DyTAG as prior TTAG research and distinguishes its embedding/distillation approach from CROSS's dynamic summaries and joint encoding. This revises the earlier unexplored-problem positioning, alongside broader coverage of recent temporal-graph and LLM-graph research in the introduction and Appendix E.

P1.justification: v2 substantially revises the introduction and method explanations, adds explicit innovation framing, and reorganizes the appendices. The parameter study moves out of the main text, the LLM ablation receives greater prominence, and robustness details receive a separate appendix. The generic impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. v2 adds Figures 10, 13, and 19 and the additional-metric Table 6, expands the LLM and cost displays, and moves retained parameter and supplementary plots. Most earlier experimental plots preserve their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The relevant LKD4DyTAG comparison, additional evaluation metrics, measured efficiency costs, and corrected dataset descriptions improve empirical completeness and transparency. These benefits outweigh limited weaknesses in the new interpretations: selected-node density plots in Appendices A and L.1 do not by themselves prove complementarity or general conflict-handling ability. The revision therefore offers a useful but bounded overall improvement.
